implementation_summary: Created the skeleton multi-device property spec file and companion fixture stub. The spec declares Identity/Device type aliases, ModelStateMD and RealSystemMD class stubs, three browser contexts in test.beforeAll (pageB authenticated first, pageA1 second with explicit SLOT_A1, pageA2 created but NOT authenticated), pubkey caches (cachedPubkeyA from pageA1, cachedPubkeyB from pageB, no cachedPubkeyA2), and a single test.describe.serial block with one placeholder test whose title contains [A15,C0] and whose body calls test.skip(true, 'S1 skeleton — body lands in S6'). The fixture file exports an awaitDeviceJoin stub that throws 'not yet implemented (S2)' to establish the import path for S2. All S1 ACs verified.

I added pubkeyA as the fourth parameter to make the helper standalone without leaking module state, but this diverges from the spec prose. lead_clarifications.question: S1 verification verdict
lead_clarifications.answer: ACCEPT (user-confirmed). The arch_violation flags (VQ-S1-003 PARTIAL sev 4, VQ-S1-016 NO sev 3, VQ-S1-015/017 PARTIAL sev 3) are all examiner-methodology artifacts: examiners checked `git diff --stat origin/master...` which surfaced commits from other already-shipped epics (epic-forget-this-device, epic-mls-live-delivery-race, relay-state hardening commit 7b31ba1, and the slot parameter shipped by epic-property-tests-l3-completion). S1's own working tree only touches the two new files it created. The `awaitDeviceJoin` 3-vs-4-param discrepancy (VQ-S1-PI-001) is an intentional carryover for S2 reconciliation. The `void(...)` unused-import suppressions (VQ-S1-PI-002) and the per-Playwright-project `--list` count (VQ-S1-PI-003) are benign and consistent with the 2-party reference. For S2+ the lead will instruct examiners to use `git diff HEAD --` rather than `git diff origin/master --` when checking scope, so phantom violations stop consuming cycles. The Decider was consulted but did not produce a textual verdict (idled twice silently); user adjudicated directly.
